title: Stop an SDK release that would break customers' builds

blocks.text: Customers build their own services against the payments SDK. Last quarter a patch release made one customer's build fail at forty call sites, and the team only heard about it from the customer. Now CI compares every public method of the release candidate with the same method in the last release, and fails the release when the new `throws` clause would stop code that compiled against the last release from compiling.
`ThrowsDiff.breaking(last, next)` already walks the candidate's throws clause and collects what it finds. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/ThrowsDiff.java`:

items: `isChecked(type)`: whether a caller must catch or declare an exception of that type;
`handledBy(type, declared)`: whether code written against a method that declared `declared` already copes with that type.

blocks.text: When you're done, CI fails a release exactly when a customer's build would, and never for a change their compiler accepts. About six lines in total.
The tests describe two versions of an SDK interface and compare their methods through reflection; `Class.isAssignableFrom` answers "is this the same type, or a supertype of that one?".

cases.says: a method that declared nothing and now declares SQLException and TimeoutException reports both, in order
a method whose throws clause did not change reports nothing
adding IllegalStateException and a subclass of IllegalArgumentException reports nothing
adding a subclass of Error reports nothing
adding Throwable and a class that extends Throwable directly reports both
declaring subclasses of an exception the last release already declared reports nothing
replacing a declared exception with its superclass reports the superclass

origin.section: Adding a Checked Exception Breaks Every Caller's Source; Adding an Unchecked One Breaks None

concepts: Adding a checked exception to a method's throws clause breaks every caller's source unless it was already handled through a supertype; adding an unchecked one breaks nothing.
Every Throwable is checked except RuntimeException, Error and their subclasses, so a class extending Throwable directly is checked.
